description: Attack the big dense shapes 6/7/11 (~100-106ms) with a NON-tridiag batched dense eigensolver that stays entirely in batched tensor-core GEMM and avoids the per-column cluster-sync wall that made the tridiag megakernel latency-bound. Try polynomial/Chebyshev spectral-filter subspace iteration: partition the spectrum into a few intervals, build a matrix polynomial band-pass filter p(A) per interval (all batched GEMM = A@X repeated), apply to a random block to extract each invariant subspace, orthonormalize (3xTF32 CQR), solve the small projected blocks, assemble. Spectrum-independent, GEMM-bound not sync-bound. Per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback. Route the n=512/1024 dense-class shapes; measure the crossover vs cuSOLVER 0.85ms/mat.

t1: Chebyshev spectral-filter subspace eigensolver (pure-GEMM, non-tridiag), routed shape-11 dense-even n=512. deg40/K8 Jackson filter + per-window CQR/Rayleigh-Ritz + membership. Validates 39/39. Shape11 339446us (3.4x regression), 640/640 fallback -- first correct-but-slow cut.

t2: fixed the Chebyshev scale bug (from-below power-iter under-scaled A -> spec exits [-1,1] -> T_k blowup; now scale=||A^2 v||*1.05), added interval-dedup + subspace-iter + global CQR2 finish. MEASURED OBSTACLE: soft window filters give individually-accurate eigenpairs (raw eig_r ~13x) but ADJACENT WINDOWS OVERLAP -> assembled Q genuinely rank-deficient, orth ~1000x gate, uncleanable without O(n^3) RR eigh. 640/640 fallback, shape11 362137us. Filter cheap+correct; cross-window orthogonality is the wall.

t3: built+measured exact sign-function multiway projectors (_cheb_sign_solve): 917ms (7 sequential sign-NS chains, 5x cuSOLVER) AND orth 1481x (16 NS iters under-converge on gapless spectrum) -> not the win. Reverted to Chebyshev filter deg120/K16/ss2. Degree/iter sweep QUANTIFIES the wall: filter converges (orth_min 50x@d200 -> 10x@d500ss3, eig_r 18->2.6x) but eigenvalue spacing 2/n forces degree O(n) to clear worst-matrix orth gate at >200ms vs cuSOLVER ~83ms floor. 640/640 fallback, shape11 712167us. nsys: filter GEMM 19%, Chebyshev-accumulation elementwise 38% (memory-bound, not TC), cuSOLVER fallback ~25%.

t4: guard the Chebyshev route OFF (_CHEB_ENABLED=False) per the brief's 'route only where it beats the current solver' rule -- the pure-GEMM filter beats nothing on shape 11 (converges but needs O(n) degree = >200ms vs cuSOLVER 83ms). Shape 11 keeps sign-DC -> geomean 28582 == parent 28611 (no regression, validates 39/39). _cheb_solve + _cheb_sign_solve machinery preserved in-tree for a follow-up brief. Final nsys confirms shape 11 back on mega_eigh_med_split_k (42%, the tridiag wall).

brief-75 (Chebyshev/pure-GEMM dense eigensolver for shapes 6/7/11) HEAD=d97df21a, geomean 28582 == parent 28611 (route guarded OFF, no regression, 39/39, 'stream' absent). 4 trials, all committed+profiled.

BUILT & MEASURED (the pure-GEMM filter IS cheap and correct-per-eigenpair): _cheb_solve = scale A->[-1,1] via A^2 power-iter + slack, slice [-1,1] into K windows, ONE shared Chebyshev-Jackson recurrence (degree d batched A@Y GEMMs, tensor-core) builds all windows' spectral-projector filters, per-window 3xTF32 CQR + Rayleigh-Ritz small batched eigh, interval-ownership dedup, membership select, sort. Routed shape 11 (lapdense_even512).

THE WALL (quantified, not argued): the filter converges to CORRECT orthonormal eigenpairs, but on the GAPLESS dense-even n=512 spectrum (eigenvalue spacing 2/n~0.004) the polynomial degree to clear the WORST matrix's ORTHOGONALITY gate is O(n): sweep gave orth_max/gate 1400x@deg40 -> orth_min(best matrix) 50x@deg200/ss2 -> 10x@deg500/ss3 (eig_r tracks 18x->2.6x). To pass all 640 matrices needs deg~1000+ x subspace-iters = >200ms of GEMM, vs cuSOLVER's ~83ms floor on shape 11. So 640/640 gate fallback at every affordable config -> regression (shape11 339-712ms). ROOT CAUSE isolated by probe: soft windows OVERLAP -> adjacent windows' bases share boundary directions -> assembled Q genuinely rank-deficient -> NS diverges, shifted-CQR2 corrupts eigvecs; the only clean orthogonalization is a global O(n^3) RR eigh == the cuSOLVER floor. Single-window probe confirmed each window captures its 67 interior eigvecs at 0.996 AND ~17 leaked boundary eigvecs -> the RR mixes boundary pairs. nsys(t3): filter A@Y GEMM 19% (tensor-core as intended), Chebyshev accumulation S+=c_k T_k 38% (memory-bound elementwise, NOT TC -- a real inefficiency if ever revived), cuSOLVER fallback ~25%.

ALSO BUILT: _cheb_sign_solve (exact sign-function multiway projectors P_{>c}=(I+sign(A-cI))/2, non-overlapping by construction, batched cuSOLVER K-blocks). MEASURED both slow (917ms: 7 sequential sign-NS chains) AND non-orthogonal (orth 1481x at 16 NS iters -- shifts land ~0.002 from eigenvalues in the gapless spectrum, NS under-converges). Not the win either.

DISPOSITION: per the brief's own guard rule ('route only where it beats the current solver'), route disabled -> parent parity. _cheb_solve + _cheb_sign_solve preserved in-tree.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not closed -- for the manager to weigh): (1) The 38% Chebyshev-accumulation elementwise cost is fixable (fold coefficients into the recurrence via Clenshaw, or accumulate via a coefficient-GEMM) -- would make the filter genuinely GEMM-bound and cheaper, though it doesn't fix the orthogonality wall. (2) The wall is SPECIFIC to the gapless even spectrum (shape 11); the MIXED shapes 6/7 contain low-rank/two-level SUBSETS a filter might resolve without the gapless-orthogonality problem -- I only tested shape 11 (the hardest). A brief targeting the filter at shape 6/7's dense-but-not-gapless subsets could avoid this wall. (3) Deflation-based windowing (build window 1, project it out, filter the deflated space for window 2, ...) gives non-overlapping subspaces by construction WITHOUT exact sign projectors -- sequential but each step is a cheap GEMM; untested. (4) A hybrid: use the CHEAP low-degree filter to build a good STARTING subspace, then hand the small reduced block to a batched Jacobi (not the tridiag megakernel) -- attacks the same 42% mega_eigh_med_split_k wall the sign-DC path has. (5) shapes 6/7/11 remain the top-3 board costs (~100-107ms each); brief-58 separately proved cuSOLVER's 0.85ms/mat is the n=1024 floor for batched paths, so shape 7 may need a fundamentally different lever than any batched decomposition.

brief-75 RESUME complete (coordinator retarget to shapes 6/7 non-gapless dense subsets + open #1/#3). HEAD=5a445c5c, geomean 28627 == parent 28611 (route disabled, no regression, 39/39, 'stream' absent, -O3). 1 new trial (total 5). The retarget lever and both extra openings were BUILT+MEASURED and all refute the filter; the result is the clean characterization the coordinator asked for.

DECISIVE MEASUREMENT -- eigenvalue-gap distributions (scaled to [-1,1]), the experiment that settles it:
 * shape 11 gapless-even: min-gap median 1.96e-3 (= uniform 2/n) -- this is the LARGEST min-gap of all three shapes.
 * shape 6 mixed-DENSE subset (264/640 mats, PR 48-62, currently low-rank k352): min-gap median 9.07e-7, median-gap 3.82e-4 -- SMALLER gaps than shape 11 (scaled-Wigner has near-degenerate pairs + clustered bulk) AND concentrated (effective rank ~55).
 * shape 7 mixed-DENSE subset: min-gap 5.33e-12 (near-degenerate).
 * shape 6/7 REST (rankdef/nearrank/rowscale): min-gap 1e-11..5e-11 (exact/near zeros).
=> The coordinator's premise (mixed dense gaps >> 0.004 so easier for the filter) is REFUTED by measurement: the mixed dense subsets are HARDER than shape 11, not easier. Ran the filter directly on shape 6's dense subset: orth_min 2471x, 264/264 fallback (vs shape 11's best orth_min 50x). And that subset already has a low-rank path at 0.126ms/mat the filter cannot approach.

DEFLATION windowing (coordinator open #3, _cheb_deflate_solve built): left->right deflate each window's filtered block against accepted eigenvectors. On shape 11 it is WORSE (orth_min 368-1835x, eig_r 108-134x vs non-deflated 50x) -- sequential deflation PROPAGATES earlier windows' boundary errors into later windows and distorts the vectors off eigenvectors. Refuted.

THE CLEAN CHARACTERIZATION (which spectra a polynomial spectral filter can/can't beat cuSOLVER on): the filter wins only where the spectrum is (a) WELL-SEPARATED (gaps >> the filter transition band pi/degree) AND (b) NOT concentrated (so windowing isn't wasted on empty [-1,1] regions). EVERY dense case on this board fails at least one: shape 11 is well-separated but UNIFORM/gapless so window edges always cut a dense region -> degree O(n) to clear the worst-matrix orth gate (>200ms vs cuSOLVER 83ms); shapes 6/7 dense subsets are CONCENTRATED with near-degenerate pairs -> tiny gaps + a cheaper low-rank path already exists. So the pure-GEMM polynomial filter has no winning shape on the current eigh board.

OPEN #1 (Clenshaw/coefficient-GEMM accumulation) NOT built this pass -- it would only cut the 38% memory-bound accumulation cost of a filter that still loses on every shape, so it does not change the conclusion; noting it for completeness.

DISPOSITION: route stays disabled (parent parity). _cheb_solve (Chebyshev-Jackson) + _cheb_sign_solve (exact sign multiway) + _cheb_deflate_solve (deflation) all preserved in-tree, fully documented, for any future brief.

REMAINING BOARD OPENINGS (not filter-related, surfaced from the shape-6 profile this pass): shape 6's dominant cost is now mega_eigh_clust_split_k (44.6%) + mega_eigh_med_split_k (14.5%) on the REST subset (rankdef/nearrank/rowscale) -> the cluster/med TRIDIAG megakernel is the shape-6 wall, same latency-bound single-CTA class brief-58/69/72 hit. Those rest matrices are rank-deficient (exact-zero gaps) so a filter won't help, but a better BATCHED small-block primitive (batched Jacobi on the reduced blocks, not the tridiag megakernel) remains open -- the same lever across shapes 5/6/11's reduced-block solves.
